title: Alto saxophone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS alto saxophone (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: Stand-in saxophone, not a measured one. No tone holes: each note is the printed mouthpiece, neck and bell cones joined by one straight cone cut to that note's length, where a real saxophone plays these notes with holes. The reed's opening, width and area are borrowed. C4 is blown at mf, E3 and F3 at ff, because they were silent at mf on this reed before the closure stop (not tried again since). One mouthpiece position, pushed in 13.27 mm and solved once on C4's passive peak on the bore air below, leaves the three at +25.6, -8.6 and -6.3 c from equal temperament (+26.4, -10.6 and -7.7 c on the pages before); the passive peaks agree to 0.3 c, so the spread is the reed's pull. All three are cleaner than the recordings, and C4's seventh harmonic sits 9 dB under its sixth. All three pages are re-renders after the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17); on the old law the reed passed through its lay on 17 to 19 % of steady samples. The duct carries a continuous gas field, Noreland 2013's measured bore-air profile of a clarinet (304.15 K at the mouthpiece to 294.96 K at the end of the clarinet's bore, exhaled breath, saturated), borrowed, with its positions scaled to the saxophone's bore by this model's choice; the body's slope and length, the three cuts and the push were re-solved on that air against equal temperament (2026-11-07) and the three pages rendered again. They score 10 of 15, 6 of 14 and 6 of 14 inside the ruler, against 10, 5 and 6: C4 and F3 tie, and E3 rises by one measure, harmonics-to-noise, as its lock falls from 1.000 to 0.978; F3's pitch moves 1.4 c toward equal temperament and away from the recording. Ab4 and E5 stay empty: with a register hole borrowed from a soprano they play an octave low.
physics_present: The printed neck (ISMA 2007), bell and mouthpiece (Lefebvre 2010) joined by one straight body cone whose slope is set once from the lowest note, Db3, and cut to each note's length, on the bore air below (slope 0.031732, a full body of 0.798097 m)
An alto reed fitted to a Lefebvre mouthpiece (Lefebvre's printed mass per area, resonance and damping); its opening 1.7 mm, width 10 mm and area 7.5e-5 m2 are borrowed
One mouthpiece position for every note, pushed in 13.27 mm, solved once on C4's passive first peak against equal temperament on the bore air below
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two alto players
Reed noise, the duct-constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990), extrapolated, with no level set against a recording
A flanged bell radiating into room air with ISO 9613 absorption, 0.5 m on axis, at 48 kHz because the engine refuses this bell at 96 kHz
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)

Bore air along the duct: Noreland 2013's measured temperature profile of a clarinet bore (304.15 K to 294.96 K, borrowed), exhaled breath with saturated water vapour, as a continuous gas field; the positions are scaled to the saxophone's bore by this model's choice (1.0783 m / 0.6552 m); the body slope, the cuts and the push are re-solved on it
physics_missing: Tone holes, pads, chimneys, key rise and a fingering chart: no measured alto air column is printed, so no hole lattice is built
A measured alto reed opening, width and area: the opening is an unplayed-tip upper bound, the width a tenor reed's and the area Lefebvre's illustrative value

The right pitch: the three sit +25.6, -8.6 and -6.3 c from equal temperament, a 34 c spread, with the passive peaks within 0.3 c of it; the spread is the reed's pull, which differs by note, and why is not shown
The recordings' spectra and noise: harmonics-to-noise reads 0.8 to 3.1 dB above the recordings on all three notes, and C4's centroid is 1164 Hz against 405 Hz
The second register: with a register hole borrowed from a soprano, placed by Scavone's rule, Ab4 and E5 sound an octave low, so they stay empty

A measured saxophone bore-air profile: the field is a clarinet's, its position scaling to the saxophone's bore is this model's choice, and E3's lock falls from 1.000 to 0.978 on this air without a traced cause
